# list_dupes

[← Command index](README.md)

List duplicate files under a directory.

## Synopsis

```
list_dupes [options]
```

## Description

Runs jdupes over the directory and all its subdirectories and prints each set of
files with identical content, with their sizes, followed by a summary of how many
duplicates there are and how much space they take. Nothing is deleted or changed.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory to search, including all subdirectories; it must exist. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### List duplicates in a directory tree

```bash
list_dupes -i ~/Downloads
```

## Notes

- jdupes must be installed with `setup_tools -k JDupes`; the command exits with an error if it is not found.
